patterns: what is a callback in conversation
entries.answer: A callback is a reference back to something said earlier, and it does two jobs at once, since it signals attention and it supplies shared ground for continuing. The reference has to be accurate, because a callback to something that was not said exposes that the listener was not listening. It also works better as a link forward than a summary back, so you did the thing I mentioned yesterday beats a recap of the previous ten minutes.

patterns: what is continuity in a conversation
why does an assistant forget context
entries.answer: Continuity is the sense that a conversation is one ongoing thing rather than a series of separate exchanges, and it is what makes a long chat feel like being with a person. It is produced by carrying context forward, and it is lost the moment the assistant treats a new message as a fresh start. The visible symptom is a question that should have been remembered being answered from scratch, which reads as though the earlier half never happened.

patterns: what does pick up the thread mean
how to change the subject back
entries.answer: A thread is the running line of a conversation, and picking one up again after a digression is the skill the word names. The failure mode is a second thread being started without the first being closed, after which neither can be resumed, and the conversation becomes a list of near-misses. A sentence that closes a digression explicitly, so going back to what you said about work, is what keeps one thread rather than five.

entries.answer: A recap summarises what has happened, and it is useful at the end of a long discussion and almost useless in the middle of one, where the listener already knows. English marks the difference in register rather than in the word, so recapping something two minutes old sounds like the speaker did not follow. The exception is a meeting with several people, where somebody genuinely was not there, and that is what a recap is actually for.

patterns: how to return to a topic
how to change the subject back smoothly
what to say when coming back
entries.answer: To return to a topic is to come back to it after a digression, and doing it explicitly is better than letting the topic die, because the alternative is that it never gets finished. The mechanics are unglamorous: name where you were, name the specific unresolved part, and continue. What does not work is announcing the return without stating where, as in back to what we were saying, since that leaves the listener doing the work.

patterns: earlier in the day vs earlier in the list
how to refer to something said before
entries.answer: Earlier is a time word that does real work in a conversation, because it is how a speaker locates something without restating it. Saying you mentioned this earlier places the point in shared history, while earlier in the day only locates it in time. The ambiguity is with the agenda, where earlier can mean previous in a list, and the fix is naming which. People use the vague version when they want to be reminded without appearing not to have been listening.
